To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
endoglin haplotypeinsufficiency results in attenuated angiogenesis and vascular remodeling, and this is due to aberrant TGF-β and VEGF signaling in endothelial cells.
endoglin haplodeficiency results in attenuation of angiogenesis in mice and human EC.

Endoglin regulates the angiogenic properties of endothelial cells via modulation of canonical and non-canonal TGFβ signaling, and that these effects are mediated by differential activation of Smad and MAPK pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of endoglin, a co-receptor for TGFβ, in angiogenesis and endothelial function.
the role of endoglin as an angiogenic modulator and the molecular mechanisms that underlie its function.
the role of endoglin during angiogenesis, and the mechanisms by which endoglin affects EC function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
endoglin haplodeficiency attenuates retinopathy and aortic angiogenesis by modulating both the pro-prolific and pro-differentiating signaling pathways in EC.
endoglin is an important regulator of endothelial cell activation during angiogenesis, and that it does so by regulating both canonical and non- canonical signaling pathways.
the endoglin haplodeficiency results in a pro-angiogenic state in EC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

endoglin haplosufficiency results in attenuated retinal neovasculature and aortas in Eng+/- mice, and that these changes in vascular development are associated with altered TGFβ/Smad and TGFβ/MAPK signaling in the endothelium.

Eng+/- EC are less responsive to TGFβ, resulting in increased VEGF expression, reduced NO production and decreased capillary morphogenesis, which collectively contribute to the attenuation of angiogenesis in Eng+/- mice.
endoglin haplodeficiency attenuates EC activation and quiesce by participating in both canonical and Smad-independent TGFβ signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endoglin is a critical regulator of endothelial cell phenotype and angiogenesis, and that its loss leads to vascular defects in the retina.
endoglin regulates the angiogenic properties of endothelial cells by participating in canonical TGFβ signaling, and by inhibiting the non-canonical TβRII/Alk1/Smad1/5 signaling pathway.
endoglin is an important regulator of EC phenotype and function.
